original_scope:
# Recovered finalized material and implemented scope

Recovered from the Cable Thermal Calculator project history, the final release-control workbook, the final Master Database and `Underground_Cable_Thermal_WebApp_COMPLETE.zip`.

| Final decision | Website behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Underground cable thermal / ampacity scope | Dedicated engineering workspace; no tray, fault, protection, grounding, voltage-drop or BOM calculators |
| Final Master Database is authoritative | Exact workbook hash, cable/source identities and thermal-relevant records preserved |
| Continuous current and conductor temperature | Retained resistance-feedback thermal network, explicit T1/T2/T3/dielectric paths, sheath and armour loss factors |
| Mutual heating and unequal circuit loads | Coupled homogeneous-soil image-source matrix; common cable construction, custom phase coordinates, up to 20 circuits and proportional/fixed-neighbor ratings |
| Parallel sets and sharing | Verified symmetry, worst-set factor or explicit set currents; unverified sharing cannot pass |
| Installations and project environment | Direct burial and screening concentric solid-filled conduit; bank, backfill, air-filled ducts and HDD/casing require verified external T4 |
| Cyclic and emergency studies | Retained four-node screening network, 24-hour profile, emergency run and incremental emergency rating |
| Soil, backfill and dry-out | Editable 2-D finite-difference domain, zones, heat sources, dry-out map and convergence output |
| Routes / crossings / HDD | Segment bottleneck, crossing temperature/rating penalties with references, screening casing or verified T4 handoff |
| Sensitivities and scenarios | Current-case comparisons with documented overrides and unchanged loss factors |
| Optimization | Thermal parameter grid and duct-position screening; selected designs need detailed recalculation |
| Case management and reporting | Device-local draft/cases, portable JSON, recalculation on restore, current printable report |
| Release status hierarchy | FAIL > INPUT REQUIRED > REVIEW REQUIRED > PASS |
| Numerical QA | 537 retained reference checks plus integration and v3 workbook audits |

The reference continuous case is 692.220438564634 A, with 55.20790930550635°C at 500 A, external T4 1.541570063174254 K·m/W and total heat 49.967131120695406 W/m. Retained emergency and field anchors are tested within the 537-check suite.

The original project's verification boundary remains: numerical regression does not certify a project. The website records construction, environment and method confirmation separately. Missing equipment data are requested for the selected product rather than borrowed from the reference example. Transient and numerical-field calculations remain screening until externally benchmarked for the project.

V3 adds structured study editors, harmonic conductor heat, robust design envelopes, condition-matched manufacturer comparisons, measured-temperature validation and reproducible advanced outputs. See `WORKBOOK_FEATURE_RELEASE.md` for formula anchors and limits.

Project and continuity: Underground cable thermal/ampacity engineering calculator and companion database, not a replacement fault, grounding, tray, protection, voltage-drop, BOM or general-purpose calculator.

Keep the original Work-chat source and all old functioning calculations, tested numerical results, reference workbooks, cases, files, diagrams, user data and project history; no silent regression or data deletion.
Use the original v3.6.2 React/TypeScript source as the engineering baseline and keep the public Wix implementation available until genuine tested replacement is possible.
One simple public URL accessible to anyone without a ChatGPT account; do not replace the existing working site with a different unrelated app.
Finish requested implementation with actual verification, not repetitive version increments or unproven completion claims.
Use all useful connected tools/plugins when justified, but do not use Formula Genius or Coursera for this project.
Preserve safe backups, full original-source copies, SHA/integrity manifests, rollback packages and a central requirements/continuation record.
Inputs, units and user experience: Default all displayed geometric distances to US feet/inches; provide selectable metric m/mm, with correct conversion both ways and canonical SI internally.
Keep unit preference synchronized across every calculator page and saved study; do not reinterpret old SI records as US values.
Fix text/controls/tables/legends/long references and report content overflowing assigned UI containers at mobile, tablet and desktop widths; shrink fonts or wrap/scroll appropriately.
Clean, professional, responsive workflow with clear inputs, outputs, charts, physical cross-sections and readable status/assumption messages.
Allow manual cable construction and database-record selection; do not invent missing equipment properties from names.
Support new/edit/delete custom cables, Excel/CSV/JSON import/export, preview, validation, provenance, duplicate ID protection and source audit.
Save/reopen/copy/delete/export complete browser-local studies; migrate legacy cases without losing numeric meaning; clear stale outputs and never trust imported approval flags.
Provide one secure, merged, integrity-checked workspace backup for saved studies and custom cables; prevent data loss on storage failures.
Provide searchable records for all 93 audited Master Database worksheets and preserve formulas, provenance, manufacturer references, original field names and full exports.
Steady and construction physics: Continuous ampacity, conductor temperature, load vs current-rating, margins, convergence and PASS/FAIL/review hierarchy.
IEC 60287-oriented loss and heat-flow paths: conductor temperature dependence, R20, AC skin/proximity, dielectric, screen/sheath, armour, T1/T2/T3 and external T4.
Direct-buried single-core, trefoil/flat/vertical/custom phase arrangement, physical spacing, burial depth, multiple circuits and unequal loads.
Explicit electrical system (three-phase AC, single-phase AC, DC), voltage rating, frequency, active conductors within cable, parallel sets and current-sharing evidence.
Sheath bonding and circulating losses, single-point/both-ends/cross-bonding; magnetic/nonmagnetic armour paths and verified limits.
Mixed cable constructions and balanced multicore thermal networks, different cable heat factors and each conductor temperature limit.
Screened conduits, solid/air fills, walls, trenches/backfill, duct banks, casings/HDD and shared banks with verified equivalent exterior thermal data.
Physical mutual heating, cable position and equivalent bank modeling, with documented model applicability.
Advanced analyses and studies: IEC 60853-oriented cyclic and emergency transient modeling, 24-hour load profile, real simulation duration, thermal masses, timestep refinement and stable initial equilibrium.
Four-node transient, emergency current scan, exact event timing and periodic-convergence checks.
2-D finite-difference soil thermal field, multiple sources, backfill rectangles, nonuniform soil, dry-out transitions and mesh/domain convergence diagnostics.
Route and crossing segment ampacity/bottleneck analysis; separate HDD/casing special-installation inputs.
Parameter sensitivity, environmental envelope, route comparisons, inverse allowable soil resistivity/spacing and candidate cable/duct-position optimization.
Harmonics and frequency-specific conductor heating, with explicit spectrum and AC resistance multipliers.
Independent manufacturer/NEC ampacity comparison only where cable identity and actual conditions match; code versus thermal criteria separated.
Measured-versus-predicted temperature validation with MAE, RMSE and maximum error by channel.
Independent IEC/IEEE/Neher–McGrath, published manufacturer, benchmark, or field validation before certified claims.
Results, reporting and QA: Traceable numerical inputs, assumptions, equations/model version, thermal resistance paths, uncertainties and source references in the report.
Full JSON/CSV/XLSX study and source exports, safe spreadsheet content, no arbitrary silent row truncation, clean native PDF/print pages.
Ten original example-case regressions plus original 537 retained reference checks; preserve all old passing cases and expand automated tests for new methods.
Fail closed for invalid geometry, material properties, missing electrical/screen/duct evidence, unstable temperature solutions or unknown selector values.
No project-approval PASS from test fixtures, imported JSON status, generic catalogue name, or an approximate method outside its stated limits.
Browser-mobile validation, real functionality/print QA, source-workbook formula mapping, source checksum comparison, release acceptance and rollback.

unanswered_questions: Which actual cable manufacturer, part number, published construction, conductor/cable voltage class and installation guide apply to each real circuit?
Are the listed source records complete, licensed for public distribution, current and duplicate-free against original manufacturer evidence?
Which cables are physically single-core, three-core, sector/segmental, screened/armoured or have different conductor load distributions?
Which screen/armour/bonding construction and independent sheath/circulation loss method is correct for the real installation?
Are actual parallel cable sets electrically balanced or is a verified worst-set/individual-load allocation needed?
What are the exact installation routes, depths, spacing/formation, ducts, banks, spare ducts, concrete/backfill structures and physical thermal interfaces?
For air-filled conduit and HDD/casings, are measured or engineering-approved gap/air coefficients and complete T4 networks available?
Which measured soil moisture/resistivity, dry-out and seasonal earth-temperature conditions govern each section?
What are the true normal, peak, emergency, cyclic and harmonic loading and permissible conductor temperatures for every cable?
What temperatures or other field data are independently available to calibrate/validate the model and thermal capacitances?
Can every source-workbook formula block be tied to a published equation and validated actual site/software result, not merely a searchable Excel formula?
Which independent IEC, manufacturer, FEM or measured benchmarks substantiate multicore, bank, HDD, dry-out, cyclic, T1/T2/T3/T4 and full Neher–McGrath applicability?
Are the specific NEC/utility/owner requirements and conductor/code ampacity correction factors defined for each project?
Has the complete original React/Next/Vinext app successfully built, deployed and passed its own live-browser parity and PDF acceptance checks?
What are the formally acceptable release tolerances, qualified engineering review criteria, owner signoff and construction-stage hold points?
Can the deployed site legally publish all raw manufacturer/research tables from the 93-sheet workbook?
Have all study-case backups stored only in past visitors’ browsers been exported? Those records are not contained in the source archives.
Are there user-shared inline-only images or attachments in older private chats that are absent from the recovered export and current file list?

Measured native/backfill/concrete/duct-fill thermal resistivities and earth temperatures (including moisture, seasonal range, sensitivity and potential dryout).
Bonding/grounding arrangements and sheath circulating/eddy loss studies, screened metal materials and electrical continuity; verification of current sharing.

Thermal capacitance/heat capacity of cable components and soil, time-history or duty profile, thermal initial state and emergency temperature constraints.

Authenticated live-original source build-and-browser evidence; audit of actual browser-local cases and complete file/source release manifests.
